outcomes: An experimenter can explicitly add the Python extension and run Python lint, test, serve, run, and dependency-install jobs through Putnami
Python dependency installation and upgrades remain scoped to explicitly configured Python workspace projects
Python integration remains usable for experiments without claiming stable compatibility, default adoption, or parity with Go or TypeScript
nonGoals: Providing a Python application framework or framework-package compatibility layer
Making Python a default workspace path
Providing feature, API, or operational parity with Go or TypeScript
Changing CLI extension discovery, workspace initialization, or upgrade orchestration

requirements.text: Documentation and generated project manifests require an explicit Python extension selection; no Python template or sample is presented as the default project path.
Python workspace installation and upgrade jobs operate on the Python projects selected from the workspace and report a skipped or failed result instead of inventing a missing project.
The extension delegates Python dependency, lint, test, and workload execution to uv, Ruff, pytest, and the configured application entrypoint, exposing their result through Putnami jobs.

Every task that runs uv requires the uv runtime toolchain bound to the uv pin of the workspace lock, so it runs and is cache-keyed on that release: uv on PATH, then toolchains/uv/uv-<version> under the Putnami home, and a uv of another release never runs. workspace-install installs the pinned release there when the machine holds none, refuses an archive whose SHA-256 differs, and declares the release as the [tool.uv] required-version of the root pyproject.toml; a hosted run installs and writes nothing.

A [tool.uv] required-version in the root pyproject.toml that names no single uv release, such as a range, or a release older than 0.11.8, the oldest one Putnami runs, fails workspace-install and every task that runs uv with a diagnostic that names the exact declaration to write, and installs and runs no uv.
The extension's support status is experimental, non-default, and unsupported for parity; upgrade documentation must not imply a supported Python framework release set.
